transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I feel like I have to keep re-checking and re-doing things before and after every drive, or else something terrible will happen and it’ll be my fault. It's just getting so overwhelming and I don't know how to make it stop.
Do you find that your struggles are a mix of both these distressing, unwanted thoughts and the physical actions you feel forced to do, or does one of them feel much more dominant than the other?

It’s definitely a mix of both because they feed into each other constantly. I get these awful mental pictures of causing a fatal crash, which forces me to do my physical checking routines to make sure everything is safe. If I don't do the checks perfectly, those looping thoughts just come right back and I have to start all over again.

Do you find yourself constantly worrying about a wide variety of everyday things, like your health, finances, or family, or is your anxiety mainly focused on these specific thoughts about driving and your checking routines?

No, it's not really about general things like my health or finances. My anxiety is almost entirely focused on my driving, specifically the fear that a small mistake on the road will cause a catastrophic accident, which forces me into these looping checking routines.
On average, how much time do you spend on these thoughts and checking routines each day? How does this affect your ability to get to places on time or go about your daily life?

These thoughts are almost constant, interrupting me even when I'm eating or trying to relax, and the checking routines take up so much time that I feel like I can barely function. It's gotten so bad that I've had to turn down lucrative driving shifts, I'm falling behind on my CDL exam prep, and I've stopped hanging out with my friends because I just don't have the time.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits a combination of both intrusive, distressing obsessive thoughts (fear of causing a fatal crash) and compulsive behaviors (repetitive physical checking routines before and after driving). These symptoms are highly time-consuming, cause significant distress, and severely impair daily functioning, including work and social activities. This presentation fits the criteria for Mixed obsessive thoughts and acts (F42.2) rather than predominantly thoughts (F42.0) or predominantly acts (F42.1).
